label: Subtraction argument: laws, omission models and the theist model
paraphrase: Premise-free comparison. Laws, for all types: the stage-one node STMT-NECESSARY-CONCRETE-AT and the box K node each exclude 'possibly no concrete object' at their world with no frame condition; the literal non-necessitation premise is S2 plus conditional subtraction; elementary existence of all candidates gives 'possibly no concrete object'; unrestricted free absence with companions at every accessible world gives S2 throughout; the analyst formulation of Lowe's reply (a non-concrete candidate existing at every accessible world, co-existing there with some concrete object; co-existence only, not grounding) excludes 'possibly no concrete object', and with S1, transitivity and excluded middle it excludes S2 and S3 holding together throughout, without choosing which fails; with excluded middle, S2 at w is equivalent to the denial of the stage-one node at w; with companions, the difference of unrestricted over contingent free absence excludes any concrete candidate existing at every accessible world. Models: all subtraction premises and the conclusion together (nonvacuity); four omission models, one per premise S1, S3, transitivity, S2, each keeping the others and falsifying the conclusion (excluded middle is not omitted: Lean is consistent with it, so no model omits it and none is needed); in the S3 model unrestricted free absence, companions and the two premises of the analyst Lowe formulation also hold and no concrete candidate is necessary; the S2 model is a theist model on an S5, hence transitive, frame in which the box K and S5 necessary-being nodes, the stage-one node, S1, S3, free absence for candidates that could be absent and companions hold, while S2 at w and throughout, unrestricted free absence and the conclusion fail. The two-being signature's divine fields are stipulated, not evidence.
